key_insight: The main driver of PV disaggregation performance is the deployment regime—who the model sees and when—not just the architecture itself.
engineering_relevance: Distribution operators should match error budgets, context length, and adaptation strategy to the intended use case: known customers, new customers, future periods, or new regions.
method: Defined four deployment regimes that separate household transfer from temporal extrapolation
Benchmarked representative deep sequence models for PV disaggregation on Ausgrid smart-meter data
Tested cross-dataset adaptation to Pecan Street with target-domain normalization and limited fine-tuning
evidence_signal: Using a fixed 48-hour context, the best model’s daylight MAE increased from 0.104 kW on seen households in the future period to 0.185 kW on unseen households, and regime choice explained more error variation than model choice.
watch_item: Results depend on the chosen deployment regime and data normalization, so field use should not assume a model that works for one customer set or region will transfer unchanged to another.
paper_title: Behind-the-Meter Photovoltaic Visibility from Net Smart Meters: Deployment Regimes and Operational Insights
